## Probe (honest input; scratch only, source `probe-close.test.ts`)

`CHAIN` is an L1 run A (0, 1000) → B (2000, 1006) carrying three finer vertices: S1 (1100, 1003) at L2, S2 (500, 1002)
at L3 and S3 (800, 1002) at L4. Each lies within 0.71 cm of every coarser route through it, and they sit on both sides
of the run. A line runs from each of them to an L0 side. On the original code, `pointLocate` and `query` agree with the
brute-force oracles in four index states: all static, all in the grid, after a stage-end rebuild, and mixed. That is
20 745 judgements per pass, with own-child answers at L3 (360) and L4 (1 038). The probe exit was 0 ("Tests 1 passed
(1)"). No wrong result was found on an honest input. The probe as a hardening fixture is note N-5.

## Verdict: FAIL — four failing lines (F-1 – F-4), all on checklist line 2; every gate is green and the code is correct on every probe

The index itself holds up. Every gate is green. The exit bar's fuzz runs clean over 6 906 batches on 200 arenas. Both of
the checker field's lines are confirmed. Every reading where the design leaves a case open is recorded in C-0160. The
checker's own probes all pass on the original code: an L0 face with no L1 record, a finer vertex off its route, and a
violation fed to each clause of the row check. The item fails because several promises it states can be broken without
any of its 46 tests turning red. Of 15 targeted mutants (J169), 3 were killed and 12 survived. All 12 survivors are
non-equivalent: the checker's probes kill the five it re-ran (A1, A3, A9, A10, A25), and each of the other seven guards
a distinct corruption that no test builds.

* **F-1 (CONFIRMED, executed).** `checkIndexBatch` is §3.10's index levels and freshness row (C-0160 (9)). It is the
  instrument of the item's only *here* bar, and it is handed to M0-a-14 to wire. Four of its promises have no red test:
  * the successor clause ("its successor lives in the grid of its current level"): mutant A1 deletes it and survives,
    also at the PR size;
  * the deleted-item clause: mutant A2 survives;
  * the coarser-write rule at its boundary: mutant A25, which tolerates a write one level coarser than the batch,
    survives (the only negative control is two levels apart, L3 → L1);
  * the demotion exceptions: mutant A26 survives; only a promoted vertex has a positive control.
* **F-2 (CONFIRMED, executed).** `checkIndexState` is asserted empty after every fuzz batch and every rebuild moment,
  and it is handed to M0-a-14. Six of its clauses can be deleted with every test still green (mutants A3 – A8). Only
  its "whose home is" clause is pinned, by query.test's forgetting writer.
* **F-3 (CONFIRMED, executed).** `pointLocate`'s own-child fallback is never exercised down to L0 (mutant A9 survives,
  also at the PR size). This is the commonest own-child case: a water face, an L0 face with no L1 record.
* **F-4 (CONFIRMED, executed).** No fixture has a finer vertex off its coarser route. Every random arena is rectilinear
  and every Steiner vertex is collinear, so reading a record on the level-n route and reading it at its own level give
  the same answers in every test. Mutant A10 (pointLocate's fallback reading the coarser record at its own level)
  survives. The checker's off-line fixture kills it, and the original code answers that fixture correctly.

```
  8000 items: pack 1.831 ms, partition rebuild 6.820 ms (design: 2.3 ms)
```

The bar holds as measured. After every batch, the row check, the whole-index state check and three oracle queries
agree. Every query also agrees across a rebuild, and rebuild work does not grow with the commits. That second half is
CONFIRMED: the stage's rebuild work is identical at 1, 8, 60 and 240 commits, and an editing session's work per commit
stays under n ÷ (threshold + 1).

How far the bar's verdict reaches is limited by F-1 and F-2. The row check's successor half, and six clauses of the
state check, have never been shown to report a violation. On those halves the bar's "holds" therefore rests on the
fuzz's oracle agreement alone. That agreement would catch a missing successor only when a random box happens to meet
it: PLAUSIBLE that the bar holds there, not CONFIRMED.

The rates are CONTENDED and reported only; nothing asserts a time, and C-0160 labels its figures so. No timing bar
belongs to this item.

## Step 5 — the failing lines, their evidence and the required changes

### §5.1 Mutants (J169: targeted, one at a time, `--maxWorkers=1`, the whole `test/index/` set)

The checker chose fifteen mutants, each aimed at a promise the author's thirty (T01 – T30, C-0160) did not visibly
target. The author's set targets the code paths; this set targets the instruments, `pointLocate`'s fallback, and the
two sort keys.

| id | file | change | aimed at | result (PLAT_FUZZ_RUNS 2000; re-run at 10 000 where marked) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | fresh.ts | `checkIndexBatch`: successor clause → `void 0` | §3.10 row: "its successor lives in the grid of its current level" | **survived** (46/46; also at 10 000) |
| A2 | fresh.ts | `checkIndexBatch`: deleted-item-in-grid clause → `if (false)` | the row on a deleted item | **survived** |
| A3 | fresh.ts | `checkIndexState`: "is in no structure" → `void 0` | every live item answered by one structure | **survived** (also at 10 000) |
| A4 | fresh.ts | `checkIndexState`: "answers from partition … and the grid" → `if (false)` | never by two structures | **survived** |
| A5 | fresh.ts | `gridProblems`: grid box holds its geometry → `if (false)` | grid entries current | **survived** |
| A6 | fresh.ts | `gridProblems`: waits for its own partition → `if (false)` | partition moves re-entered | **survived** |
| A7 | fresh.ts | `checkIndexState`: home's partition answers → `if (false)` | home entry current | **survived** |
| A8 | fresh.ts | `checkIndexState`: grid holds no dead item → `if (false)` | no stale grid entry | **survived** |
| A9 | query.ts | `pointLocate` fallback loop `m >= 0` → `m >= 1` | the own-child record named down to L0 (C-0160 (5)) | **survived** (also at 10 000) |
| A10 | query.ts | fallback reads `faceRouteRings(p, lm, slot, lm)` instead of `(…, level)` | the coarser record read on the level-n route (§3.3) | **survived** (also at 10 000) |
| A11 | spatial.ts | `gridInsert`: drop the old partition share's delete | a replaced entry leaves its old partition | killed (fuzz) |
| A19 | query.ts | edge sort on the lower endpoint only | §3.3's edge key, no structure-order tie-break | killed (11 tests) |
| A20 | query.ts | face sort on the key's first vertex only | §3.3's face key, no structure-order tie-break | killed (2 tests, incl. the allocation-order test) |
| A25 | fresh.ts | coarser-write rule `w.level >= log.level` → `>= log.level - 1` | "no index of a level coarser than its own" at its boundary | **survived** (also at 10 000) |
| A26 | fresh.ts | the demoted-edge exception → `false` | "except the promotions and demotions it made" | **survived** |

Equivalence was checked by probes on the original code, in a scratch-mirror test file outside the tree:
* **P1 (L0 own child).** On M0-a-02's `LAKE` arena, `pointLocate` of (1000, 1000) at L1 – L4 gives
  `{ on: 'face', level: 0, face: <the lake> }`.
* **P2 (off-line finer vertex).**
  * The fixture `OFFLINE` is an L0 square 0 – 1000 with an L1 line A (0, 500) → B (1000, 503), whose ends are Steiner
    vertices on the L0 sides. S (500, 501) is an L2 vertex on that run, 0.5 cm off its straight route. An L2 line runs
    S → T (500, 0). The upper L1 face holds no L2 record.
  * Queries agree with the test support's `oracleQuery` at every level, all static and all in the grid, over point and
    3 × 1 boxes near S.
  * `pointLocate` at L2 of (400, 501) names the upper L1 record: A–S there is 500.8 and A–B 501.2. At L1 the same point
    lies in the lower L1 face.
* **P3 (row and state checks).**
  * A changed L2 item tombstoned and not re-entered: `checkIndexBatch` reports "in no grid" and `checkIndexState`
    reports "in no structure".
  * An L2 batch writing the L1 index is reported.

All five probe tests pass on the original code (exit 0, "Tests 5 passed (5)"). Run alone against the mutants, they kill
A1, A3, A9, A10 and A25: each "1 failed | 4 passed (5)". Those five survivors are therefore CONFIRMED non-equivalent.

A2 and A4 – A8 each guard a distinct corruption: a freed slot left in the grid, an item answering from both
structures, a stale grid box, a wrong pending partition, a home naming a partition that does not hold the item, and a
dead grid entry. No test builds any of these. They are non-equivalent by reading (PLAUSIBLE), and each needs one
negative control.

A26: the vertex half of the exception has a positive control (`promoted: [v]`), but neither demoted vertices nor
demoted edges do.

### F-1 — the §3.10 row check's clauses cannot fail in any test (checklist line 2)

* **Evidence.** A1, A2, A25 and A26 survive. The only negative controls are fuzz.test's "one changed item … left
  untombstoned", which hits the tombstone clause, and "a batch writes an index coarser than its own", an L3 batch
  writing L1, which hits a two-level gap.
* **Required change**, in `packages/kernel/test/index/` (fuzz.test.ts or a new test file):
  * a negative control for each clause of `checkIndexBatch`:
    * a changed item tombstoned whose successor is not inserted, reporting "in no grid of its level";
    * a deleted item whose slot was freed while its grid entry stayed, reporting "still in the L*n* grid";
    * an L2 batch writing the L1 index, reporting "an L2 batch wrote the L1 index";
  * positive controls for the demotion exception: the same coarser vertex write accepted when the vertex is named in
    `demoted.vertices`, and an edge write accepted when its pair is named in `demoted.edges` (and refused when it is
    not).

  Each must turn A1, A2, A25 or A26 red.

### F-2 — six clauses of the whole-index state check cannot fail (checklist line 2)

* **Evidence.** A3 – A8 survive. `checkIndexState` is asserted `[]` after every fuzz batch and every rebuild moment,
  and C-0160 (9) hands it to M0-a-14. Only its "whose home is" clause has a red test (query.test, "a writer that frees
  a slot without its tombstone").
* **Required change.** One corruption per clause, each asserting its message:
  * a live item tombstoned and not re-entered ("is in no structure");
  * an item put in the grid (`gridPut` directly) while its static copy is untombstoned ("answers from partition … and
    the grid");
  * a vertex moved after its grid entry was written ("grid box does not hold its geometry");
  * a regroup without re-entry ("waits for partition");
  * a home entry naming a partition that does not hold the item ("does not answer for it");
  * a grid entry for a freed slot ("no live item of the level").

  Each must turn its mutant (A3 – A8) red.

### F-3 — `pointLocate`'s fallback to an L0 own child is untested (checklist line 2)

* **Evidence.** A9 survives at the PR size. pointlocate.test's own-child case is an L2 record seen from L4 (QUARTERS'
  south-east quarter). The random arenas almost never leave an L0 face unrefined. Yet water faces, L0 faces with no L1
  record, are the commonest own-child case, and §3.4's cross-arena readers locate points in them.
* **Required change.** A `pointLocate` case on an arena with an L0 face that holds no L1 record, such as M0-a-02's
  `LAKE` arena (`test/arena/support.ts`, already importable). The lake's point (1000, 1000) at L1 – L4 must give
  `{ on: 'face', level: 0 }`, both all static and through the grid. It must turn A9 red. The original code passes it
  (P1).

### F-4 — no fixture puts a finer vertex off its coarser route (checklist line 2)

* **Evidence.** A10 survives at the PR size. Every random arena is rectilinear on a 10 cm grid. `splitPair` places
  off-segment points only when an edge has no interior lattice point, which never happens there. The hand-built
  fixtures' finer vertices all lie exactly on their routes: PLOTS' s (100, 30) lies on c–e.

  So §3.3's "read on the level-n route" is never distinguished from a reading at the record's own level, and the
  0.71 cm padding is held only by box-value equality in items.test. No query ever depends on it, although §3.3's
  route-edge items exist for exactly that case (J-K32).
* **Required change.** An off-line fixture, such as the checker's `OFFLINE` arena in §5.1 P2, added to:
  * the oracle-agreement tests (points and small boxes around the off-line vertex, static and through the grid);
  * pointlocate.test: (400, 501) at L2 → the upper L1 record (own child at L2), at L1 → the lower L1 face.

  It must turn A10 red. The original code passes it (P2).

### Notes (not failing)

* **N-1 (CONFIRMED by grep inside `plat/`; for the session).** No table holds `index.gridCellM`.
  `packages/tables/data/lattice.json` has `arena` and `route` only, and the string occurs nowhere in `plat/` outside the
  item's files, the work file and the ledger row. C-0160 (3) makes the cell the caller's, and the design's value lies in
  V11 §3.1, which no M0 seat may read. The first caller of `attachIndex` (M0-a-16's façade or the spikes) will need a
  sourced value or a choices row. Route it to the spec lane, or to that item's brief.
* **N-2 (CONFIRMED by reading `vendor/flatbush@4.6.2/index.js:73`).** The adapter's header calls §2.2's
  `PackedIndex` "a 32-bit index per node … the library's defaults, fixed here". In fact flatbush picks `Uint16Array`
  indices below 16 384 nodes (`numNodes < 16384 ? Uint16Array : Uint32Array`). adapter.test checks 38.4 B per item
  only at 20 000 items. No output depends on this. It matters only for M1's frozen-copy size accounting (§3.3 pool step
  1: "38.4 B per item"). The comment should say so in the fix round.
* **N-3 (equivalent by reading).** `rebuildForFreeze`'s two emptiness assertions cannot fire after a correct
  `rebuildDirty`. A mutant removing them is equivalent while `rebuildDirty` is correct; no test is needed.
* **N-4 (PLAUSIBLE, no impact at M0).** Partition numbers follow the order in which each partition key is first met:
  at `attachIndex`, levels in order and items in slot order. They are kernel-internal, held only in `indexHome`, and
  read by no output: every answer is sorted by position. M1's pool merge, where the home column takes the overlays'
  partition numbers (§3.3 pool step 4), should keep them out of every output.
